newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says German M3 slowed markedly in June vs May.
newsitem.headline: Buba says German M3 slowed markedly in June vs May.

text.p: Germany's Bundesbank said on Monday that growth in the M3 measure of money supply slowed markedly in June compared to May, with reduced lending and stronger monetary capital formation behind the trend change.
The German central bank said in a statement that cash in circulation nonetheless increased significantly in the month.
The Bundesbank also noted that for the first time this year German non-banks were seeing inflows of funds from their dealings with foreign institutions.
Aside from an increase in cash in circulation, the central bank also noted a build-up in savings desposits with three-month maturities, while on-demand and shorter-term deposits decreased.

The M3 money supply measure, which is the Bundesbank's main policy indicator, rose by 6.4 percent in June compared to 7.0 percent in May, thus falling within the central bank's 1997 target range of 3.5 to 6.5 percent.
Economists polled by Reuters on average had expected M3 growth in June to have slowed to 6.8 or 6.9 percent versus the final quarter of 1996.
For the six-month period between December and May, M3 growth on a seasonally-adjusted basis stood at 6.5 percent.
